title: E2F1 Suppresses EBV Lytic Reactivation through Cellular and Viral Transcriptional Networks
authors: Biswas J; Ali SA; Malik S; Nag S; Mukherjee P; Saha A
one_liner_zh: 该文研究E2F1与BZLF1在EBV潜伏-裂解转换中的转录调控网络，属基因表达调控而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联弱。
abstract:
Latent EBV infection is causally associated with various B-cell malignancies, while periodic lytic-cycle replication is essential for sustaining viral progeny. Lytic cycle induction represents a promising therapeutic strategy for EBV-associated neoplasms. Therefore, uncovering the mechanisms that regulate EBV lytic-cycle reactivation is pivotal for understanding viral pathogenesis and advancing novel therapies. Our genome-wide transcriptomic analysis reveals that E2F1 expression is transcriptionally activated during EBV latent infection in B-lymphocytes but significantly suppressed during lytic cycle reactivation. While ectopic E2F1 expression suppresses lytic replication, E2F1 depletion markedly accelerates this process. Mechanistically, we establish that E2F1 and the lytic transactivator BZLF1 form a negative transcriptional feedback loop, tightly controlling viral lytic replication. Furthermore, E2F1 positively regulates c-Myc expression and together they repress the leaky BZLF1 expression during latency. Importantly, c-Myc does not influence E2F1 expression, nor does BZLF1 modulate c-Myc transcription, underlining a distinct regulatory hierarchy. In sum, our findings reveal that EBV tightly controls the latent-to-lytic switch through precise regulation of E2F1 expression, positioning E2F1 as a pivotal regulator of both cellular and viral gene expression.

Synopsis

EBV coordinates the latent-to-lytic switch by sensing E2F1 abundance, which acts as a crucial transcriptional regulator of both cellular and viral gene expressions. During EBV latent infection, E2F1 promotes c-Myc transcription, and together they suppress EBV lytic cycle transactivator BZLF1 expression. E2F1 and BZLF1 form a negative feedback loop in order to control each other’s transcriptions. BZLF1-driven controlled E2F1 expression successively inhibits c-Myc level, thereby stimulating EBV lytic cycle reactivation. BZLF1 does not regulate c-Myc, nor does c-Myc reciprocally regulate E2F1, emphasizing a unidirectional regulatory hierarchy.
abstract_zh:
潜伏性EBV感染与多种B细胞恶性肿瘤存在因果关联，而周期性裂解周期复制对于维持病毒后代至关重要。裂解周期诱导代表了一种针对EBV相关肿瘤的有前景的治疗策略。因此，揭示调控EBV裂解周期再激活的机制，对于理解病毒发病机制和推进新型疗法至关重要。我们的全基因组转录组分析揭示，在B淋巴细胞中EBV潜伏感染期间，E2F1表达被转录激活，但在裂解周期再激活期间显著抑制。虽然异位E2F1表达抑制裂解复制，但E2F1缺失显著加速此过程。机制上，我们确定E2F1和裂解反式激活因子BZLF1形成负转录反馈环，紧密调控病毒裂解复制。此外，E2F1正向调控c-Myc表达，且二者共同在潜伏期抑制泄漏性BZLF1表达。重要的是，c-Myc不影响E2F1表达，BZLF1也不调节c-Myc转录，这突显了一种独特的调控层级。总之，我们的发现揭示，EBV通过精确调控E2F1表达来紧密控制潜伏期至裂解期的转换，将E2F1定位为细胞和病毒基因表达的关键调控因子。

摘要

EBV通过感知E2F1丰度来协调潜伏期至裂解期的转换，E2F1作为细胞和病毒基因表达的关键转录调控因子。在EBV潜伏感染期间，E2F1促进c-Myc转录，且二者共同抑制EBV裂解周期反式激活因子BZLF1表达。E2F1和BZLF1形成负反馈环以控制彼此的转录。BZLF1驱动的受控E2F1表达依次抑制c-Myc水平，从而刺激EBV裂解周期再激活。BZLF1不调节c-Myc，c-Myc也不反向调节E2F1，强调了一种单向调控层级。
